title: Victoria Road South zoning approval for 486 homes
subtitle: Neighbourhood feedback on site plan, parking and traffic concerns, electric vehicle charging, and the mayor's response to the Premier
overview: Council approved a zoning by-law amendment for 855 and 927 Victoria Road South {{vote:m1}}. It allows 486 homes: 183 townhouses and two ten-storey apartment buildings with 303 units. The lands were already designated for medium and high density, and no Official Plan change was requested. Several councillors said they had reservations but that limited grounds to refuse made an appeal likely to succeed.

Council also directed staff to invite the McAlister Neighbourhood Group to view and give feedback on the site plan {{vote:m2}}. This is an invitation, not a Planning Act requirement. Residents said the area lacks walkable shops and frequent transit. They also raised concerns about parking, traffic, building height next to rural lands, and natural heritage.

The developer's team said electric vehicle charging will be provided on the south parcel. The developer will fund new traffic signals on Victoria Road. Council also passed three by-laws {{vote:m3}}. After the vote, the mayor made a statement responding to recent comments by the Premier about Guelph's council and its record on housing. No motion was attached to it.

decisions.detail: Council approved site-specific zoning to permit 486 homes, made up of 183 townhouses and two ten-storey apartment buildings with 303 units, and found no further public notice was needed for minor changes.
Council directed staff to invite the McAlister Neighbourhood Group to view and comment on the site plan for the development.

debate: Delegates from the neighbourhood said the development is too dense and too tall for a rural edge. They questioned two ten-storey buildings facing rural lands across Victoria Road. They noted the unit count had grown since the 2019 public meeting.

Residents said the area is not walkable, with no nearby shops, limited transit and a school at capacity. They expected most residents to rely on cars and said traffic on neighbourhood streets and Victoria Road would increase. One delegate said the parking supply falls short of the by-law requirement.

One councillor questioned the narrower parking spaces, the missing charging provisions for the south block, the small amenity spaces and the shortfall in parking. Staff said the parking was supported by a consultant study, and that required parking has to be provided on site.

Several councillors said they disliked parts of the design but that the land was long designated for high density. They noted that refusing would risk a costly appeal, citing a previous case. One councillor voted against, saying the site's setting near protected groundwater lands makes it a poor fit for high-rises, and stressed this was not opposition to housing.

The developer's representatives said the density was moved toward Victoria Road to reduce shadowing on neighbouring townhouses. They said smaller units respond to demand for entry-level homes, and that parking is above ground because of the water table.
